result.topic_en: Part of an expert report (Gutachten) on geodesy. It argues that the exact figure of the Earth can be determined once connected triangulations, refined astronomical latitude and longitude determinations, and systematic gravity measurements are available. It holds that the scientific evaluation of these data should be left to the free judgement of whoever undertakes it.

items.english: In our view it cannot fail that this higher scientific aim will be fully achieved once, through combined efforts, the necessary foundations have been procured and made generally known. These are: 1) connected triangulations; 2) completed and refined astronomical determinations of latitude and longitude; and, as we add following what is said in the appendix, 3) equally systematically executed gravity determinations.

items.english: Drawing from these foundations, with full scientific rigour, all the conclusions about the figure of the Earth that can be taken from them seems to us an indivisible, purely scientific task. Whoever undertakes it must be granted full freedom, so good advice but no binding prescriptions would seem admissible. For this reason probably nobody should be charged with directing this work.
